title: Tiko-Ta
prompt:
Original sunny bubblegum K-pop / tropical dance-pop song for a family rhythm-platform game, playful, sparkling, irresistibly bouncy. Completely new melody and arrangement. Full finished compact song, approximately 90 seconds, not a preview. Steady 132 BPM, 4/4, fixed tempo throughout.

Tight punchy kick, crisp snare and handclaps, clearly audible downbeats, buoyant melodic bass, bright tropical plucks and light marimba, warm polished synth chords. Rhythmic vocal accents must be very clear and separated. Give the groove space: short rests between motifs, occasional held notes lasting 1–2 beats and one small rhythmic break before the last chorus. Cheerful modern pop production that children and teenagers can enjoy.

Lead vocal: warm youthful friendly cartoon-character singing, melodic and expressive, clean consonants, comfortable mid/high register, natural smiling timbre with gentle studio polish. No shrill baby voice, no animal noises, no speech, no English or other meaningful words. All sung vocals consist ONLY of invented syllables below. Tiko is pronounced TEE-koh, ta is TAH, piki-pa is PEE-kee-PAH. Main hook: "Tiko-ta"; short answering hook: "piki-pa". Verses must have melodic variation, not one phrase repeated mechanically. A light doubled voice can answer the lead in the chorus. Do not sing section labels.

Compact arrangement around 48 bars: 2-bar rhythmic intro; 8-bar verse; 8-bar chorus; 8-bar varied second verse; 4-bar airy break with held syllables; 16-bar final chorus with melodic variations; 2-bar resolving outro and brief reverb tail. Finish with a proper musical ending around 90 seconds; no long intro, no long instrumental solo, no extended fade.
